title: DES DECam images show a pre-discovery ASASSN-14ko flare in December 2013; its time excludes a constant period before 2016 and favours a period decrease that is modulated every 19 orbits
abstract: Question: the period history of the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko (2007-2026) has no flare time between 2008 and 2014. Clocks that fit the other data differ most in this gap: an episodic clock (slow decrease, fast decrease in 2018-2020, stall in 2020-2024), clocks with a constant period before 2016, and a steady decrease with a periodic O-C term. Approach: we found seven DES DECam nights from 2013 November 15 to 2014 February 7, 11 months before discovery, in Legacy Surveys DR10. We did PSF-matched photometry of the nucleus, timed the flare with 12 ASAS-SN g flare templates, and refitted the clock models of SCI 067e9565 (four timing sets; out-of-sample tests; bootstrap). Results: on 2013 December 23 to 2014 January 4 the nucleus was 8-13 percent brighter in z, g and r than on 2013 November 15 and 2014 January 31-February 7. The excess is a point source 0.3-0.45 arcsec from the Gaia DR3 north nucleus and 1.1 arcsec from the companion nucleus. It is flare n = -2: half-rise MJD 56642.0 (68 percent 56635.3-56648.8; seven variants give medians 56640-56648); X-ray-dip-equivalent time 56637.4 +/- 6.3 for a 4.75-d lag. All clocks fitted without it predict it too early: by 28.9 d for clocks with a constant period before 2016 (z = 4.5), 16.4 d for the best episodic clock (z = 2.5), 8.6 d for a constant Pdot and 7.0 d for the modulated clock (z = 1.1). After the refit the constant-period-before-2016 clocks are worse by Delta AIC = 21-25, the episodic clock by 5.0-9.7 (bootstrap p = 0.01 if it is true), and the modulated clock is best; the modulation period is 18.8-19.7 cycles (5.6-5.9 yr), and the 36-cycle alias is removed. The mean period was 116.0 +/- 0.4 d in 2008-2013, 111.6 +/- 0.6 d in 2013-2016, about 112 d in 2016-2018 and 108.5 d in 2020-2024: two drops of about 4 d, about 20 orbits apart. Conclusion: the 2020-2024 stall is the second plateau of a repeated drop-and-plateau pattern, not a unique switch-off. If the modulation is general-relativistic apsidal precession, the pericentre is at 29 or 57 gravitational radii. Forecast: flare-41 dip 2026 November 3 (modulated) against November 21 (constant X-ray clock). Limitations: one flare sampled after its rise; the time rests on template decline shapes and an assumed 2013 lag; the relaxed 2015-2017 V-band set still prefers the episodic clock, which then misses this flare by 2.9 sigma; the modulation is phenomenological.
